heard: a city-killer asteroid hid in plain sight until just before impact. In July 2019, 2019, O.K. screamed past us at nearly 55,000 miles per hour. The football-field-sized rock missed our planet by about 45,000 miles. That is less than one-fifth of the distance to the moon. An impact would have released over 30 times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb. Survey telescopes like PanestiARRS had actually photographed it earlier, but it went unrecognized. Because the asteroid was heading directly toward us, it appeared completely stationary. Amateur astronomers Jacques, Pimentel, and Ribeiro finally spotted the threat before its approach. This Apollo-class rock won't return for 200 years, but it proved how a city-killer asteroid hid in plain sight.
